name: Fieberbrunn
kurzbeschreibung: The gateway to Saalbach-Hinterglemm – 200 kilometers of ski runs and the legendary snowboard events.
beschreibung:
Overview

Fieberbrunn is located at an altitude of 790 meters in the eastern reaches of North Tyrol in the Pillerseetal valley, within the district of Kitzbühel. Home to roughly 4,400 residents, this historic market town is the largest municipality in the valley, nestled picturesquely between the rolling Kitzbühel Alps and the jagged limestone massifs of the Loferer and Leoganger Steinberge. Renowned internationally as a vibrant alpine sports resort, Fieberbrunn forms a vital link in the expansive Skicircus Saalbach Hinterglemm Leogang Fieberbrunn arena. In summer, the valley enchants visitors with pristine alpine waters such as Lake Wildseelodersee, thrilling family adventure parks, and an intriguing heritage of historic iron mining.

History

Originally documented in 1156 under the name Pramau, derived from the Old High German term for blackberry bush, the town's current name stems from a legendary royal cure. In 1354, Countess Margarete Maultasch, sovereign ruler of Tyrol, fell severely ill with persistent fever. After drinking the sulfurous waters of the spring below the church hill, she recovered completely within days. In gratitude, the locals renamed the healing fountain and the settlement Fieberbrunn (literally Fever Well); today, an expressive bronze sculpture of the countess adorns the market square fountain. Beginning in the fifteenth century, Fieberbrunn developed into a thriving center for iron ore mining and metallurgy, producing high-grade Pillersee steel. Rising proudly above the town, the parish church of Saints Primus and Felician features Late Gothic origins dating back to 1445, enhanced by exquisite eighteenth-century rococo stucco ornamentation.

Getting There

By automobile from Germany, travel proceeds via motorway A93 to the Kufstein-Süd exit, continuing along federal road B173 to St. Johann in Tirol and taking the B164 directly into Fieberbrunn; a toll-free alternative runs via Kössen. From Salzburg and eastern Austria, route B164 leads through Lofer and Waidring. Rail travelers benefit from Fieberbrunn's dedicated station on the Salzburg-Tyrol railway line, served by frequent S-Bahn (S8) and Regional Express trains connecting directly to Wörgl, Innsbruck, and Salzburg. Locally, the Pillerseetal regional bus connects all village districts and gondola terminals every half hour, free of charge for holders of the Kitzbühel Alps guest card.

Tips

In winter, the Fieberbrunn cable cars provide seamless access to the massive Skicircus network spanning 270 kilometers of interconnected ski slopes. Internationally celebrated as a freeride sanctuary, Fieberbrunn hosts the prestigious Freeride World Tour on the razor-sharp north face of Mount Wildseeloder (2,118 m). During summer, an unforgettable alpine hike leads up to the deep-blue Lake Wildseelodersee at 1,854 meters, home to the historic Wildseeloderhaus refuge and pedal boating at high altitude. Families will love the Streuböden mid-station, featuring Timoks Wilde Welt adventure park and the year-round Timoks Alpine Coaster toboggan. A visit to the nearby Buchensteinwand reveals the monumental, walk-in Jakobskreuz cross.
